title: Filtered colimits of flat module sheaves are flat
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small in a coefficient universe $w$, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on it, and let $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ denote sheaves of $R$-modules with section groups in $w$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I$ be a $w$-small nonempty directed poset (any two elements have a common upper bound), and let $(P_i,p_{ij})_{i\le j}$ be a diagram in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Suppose every $P_i$ is flat, meaning that the sheaf tensor functor $P_i\otimes_R-$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $q_i:P_i\to P$ is any colimit cocone in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], then $P$ is flat. In particular, for every finite diagram $D$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, the canonical comparison
$$P\otimes_R\lim D\ \longrightarrow\ \lim(P\otimes_R D)$$
is an isomorphism, including when $D$ is empty. No sectionwise-flatness or enough-points hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03EU (lemma-colimits-flat), part (2), filtered-colimit clause, and its proof citing Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits). Serves lem-sfb-qlbar-flat.proof.md tensor-colimit sentence and final exactness sentence; extracts live proof steps 3-5.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Since the site is $w$-small, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies in universe $w$ and makes $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck abelian. Morphisms are families of sectionwise linear maps indexed by the $w$-small site, hence have $w$-small sets. The nonempty directed poset $I$ is filtered by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits] gives all required $w$-small limits and colimits in $\mathcal A$, and says that $\operatorname{colim}_I:\mathcal A^I\to\mathcal A$ preserves finite limits. All subsequent colimits are in $\mathcal A$, not presheaf or sectionwise colimits.

source.place: Tag 03EU, proof of (2), exactness of filtered colimits; Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits.

proof.text: For every $X\in\mathcal A$, [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] applied to $X\otimes_R-$ sends the given cocone $(P,q_i)$ to a colimit cocone. The symmetry in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identifies this diagram and cocone with $(P_i\otimes_R X,q_i\otimes1_X)$. Consequently the canonical map $\alpha_X:\operatorname{colim}_i(P_i\otimes_R X)\to P\otimes_R X$ is an isomorphism, with $\alpha_X\iota_{i,X}=q_i\otimes1_X$. For $f:X\to Y$, both composites from $\operatorname{colim}_i(P_i\otimes_R X)$ to $P\otimes_R Y$ agree after each $\iota_{i,X}$ by tensor functoriality; colimit uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore proves naturality of $\alpha$ in $X$.

Let $K$ be a finite category, $D:K\to\mathcal A$, and $(L,\pi_k)$ a limit cone. By flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], each tensor functor is exact, in particular it preserves finite limits; symmetry [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] allows the factor $P_i$ on the left. Hence the canonical $\gamma_i:P_i\otimes_R L\to\lim_k(P_i\otimes_R D(k))$, characterized by projection $1_{P_i}\otimes\pi_k$, is an isomorphism. For $i\le j$, the two maps expressing compatibility of $\gamma_i$ and $\gamma_j$ have the same $k$-projection, namely $p_{ij}\otimes\pi_k$, so limit uniqueness proves compatibility. Thus the $\gamma_i$ form an isomorphism of $I$-diagrams; its inverse is the family of inverses, whose naturality follows by composing the same equality with the inverses.

source.place: Tag 03EU, hypothesis that the stage sheaves are flat; Tag 03ER, definition-flat, item (3).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits] to the bifunctor $(i,k)\mapsto P_i\otimes_R D(k)$, using the Grothendieck category and sizes from Step 1. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\beta:\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_k(P_i\otimes_R D(k))\to\lim_k\operatorname{colim}_i(P_i\otimes_R D(k))$. Compose the following isomorphisms:
$$P\otimes_R L\xrightarrow{\alpha_L^{-1}}\operatorname{colim}_i(P_i\otimes_R L)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{colim}_i\gamma_i}\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_k(P_i\otimes_R D(k))\xrightarrow{\beta}\lim_k\operatorname{colim}_i(P_i\otimes_R D(k))\xrightarrow{\lim_k\alpha_{D(k)}}\lim_k(P\otimes_R D(k)).$$
The colimit and limit of the displayed isomorphisms are isomorphisms because the corresponding functors send their inverse families to inverse maps. Denote this composite by $\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 03EU, proof of (2), using exact filtered colimits; Tag 03DB, finite-limit formulation of exactness.

proof.text: For $k\in K$, precompose the $k$-projection of $\kappa$ with $q_i\otimes1_L=\alpha_L\iota_{i,L}$. By the defining projections of $\beta$ and $\gamma_i$ the result is $(q_i\otimes1_{D(k)})(1_{P_i}\otimes\pi_k)=(1_P\otimes\pi_k)(q_i\otimes1_L)$. The maps $q_i\otimes1_L$ are colimit legs by Step 2, so colimit uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies the $k$-projection of $\kappa$ with $1_P\otimes\pi_k$. Limit uniqueness then identifies $\kappa$ with the canonical comparison in the statement. This proves its invertibility. When $K$ is empty, Step 4 still applies: preservation of finite limits includes the terminal object, and the same cone uniqueness has no projection equations to check. Thus the empty-diagram clause is included.

source.place: Tag 03EU, proof of (2); universal properties identifying the canonical finite-limit comparison.

proof.text: Finally [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] and the symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] show that $P\otimes_R-$ also preserves all $w$-small colimits, hence finite colimits. Steps 3–5 show that it preserves finite limits. It is therefore exact (left and right exact), and symmetry gives the same property for $-\otimes_R P$. This is precisely flatness in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The argument used sheaf tensor products and Grothendieck exactness throughout and required neither points of the site nor sectionwise flatness.
